title: 2025-08-26 Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache (Novafinance)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-08-26
- Time: 09:34 PDT
- Duration: ~58 min
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aisha (Novafinance Head of ML), Mark (Platform), Priya (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): walkthrough of Redwood Optimize focusing on batching and caching, some cost numbers, pilot agreed.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, with Lena and Diego from the SE team. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Aisha: Good morning. Excited to see the cost stuff — we've been hitting token costs that are higher than expected.
00:20 Mark: Yeah we're trying to nail down cost per inference for our fraud-screening flows.
00:28 Samir: Great, our plan today is to walk through batching strategies, prefix vs KV cache, and a tailored cost model for your workload. We'll pause for Qs.
00:39 Lena: Quick note — when I say KV cache, some docs call it key-value or next-token cache, sometimes prefix cache is used interchangeably; we'll highlight differences.
00:53 Priya: Important for us: security, VPC, KMS. We'll need SOC2 docs and audit log details.
01:02 Samir: Yep, we'll share SOC 2 and our security whitepaper; we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
01:15 Aisha: Our SLO is sub-200ms 95th for the live scoring path, but we can tolerate slightly higher for backfill/batch.
01:25 Diego: Noted. Can you share typical sequence lengths and tokens per request? That changes batching and KV efficiency a lot.
01:34 Aisha: Average sequence around 120 tokens, 95th ~480. Many requests have identical prefixes — the first 40-80 tokens are template prompts.
01:45 Lena: That's great — prefix cache will help a lot when the prefix repeat rate is high. We'll demonstrate numbers.
01:52 Samir: I'll pull up the cost model.
02:10 [screen share noise]
02:15 Lena: Ok, slide 1 — high level: continuous batching improves GPU utilization but increases tail latency; prefix cache reduces total generated tokens per request by reusing cached KV state when the prefix matches. KV cache helps for partial matches and multistep dialogs.
02:33 Mark: How much does batching typically reduce cost? ballpark numbers?
02:39 Lena: On throughput-heavy workloads, batching can reduce per-token cost by 20-40% depending on GPU and model. For your mix (120 avg token, high concurrency), we expect 25-30% unit cost savings with 64-128 batch sizing under Redwood Dedicated.
02:56 Samir: Important nuance — aggressive batching can inflate p95 latency. We typically suggest latency-aware batching: target a soft SLO on p95, and configure max_batch_delay to cap wait time.
03:12 Aisha: So we get cost wins but keep 95th under 200ms? Sounds tight.
03:19 Lena: For single-token generation steps it's tough. But because your prefix repeats, prefix cache cuts generation tokens — often >40% token reduction — which translates to latency and cost wins without large batching.
03:34 Priya: Can you explain prefix vs KV cache again? We heard KV cache keeps everything in memory, prefix cache is more like caching model attention outputs?
03:44 Diego: TL;DR: prefix cache stores whole KV state for exact prefix hashes — it's super fast for exact matches. KV cache (as we called it here) can do prefix-subset reuse and partial matches; it's more memory intensive but captures more reuse across slightly differing prompts. Sometimes teams use both: prefix cache for exact high-frequency templates + lightweight KV for near-matches.
04:08 Mark: Memory implications? Our Dedicated nodes are 80GB GPU mem (A100-class).
04:15 Lena: Depends on model size and KV footprint. For a 7B model, KV per token is small; for 70B the KV grows. We showed a sample table: per-active-session KV ~ 2-8MB per 100 tokens (approx), so plan capacity accordingly.
04:36 Aisha: Do you have quantized model suggestions? We run in Dedicated and want lower cost while preserving quality.
04:43 Samir: Optimize recommends model and quantization based on evals. For sensitive scoring you might keep FP16 on critical paths, and use int8/4 for lower cost internal batch jobs. We'll include recommended profiles in the spreadsheet.
05:00 [brief crosstalk]
05:12 Lena: Now cost model slide. I'm opening the spreadsheet: column A request type, columns for avg tokens, repeat prefix rate, batching assumptions, and resulting tokens generated, GPU time, and unit cost.
05:27 Lena: Example row: real-time scoring: avg tokens 120, prefix match rate 40%, batch size 16, expected per-request generated tokens ~72, unit cost $0.018 per request. If prefix cache is 60% match, tokens drop to ~48, cost down to $0.012.
05:47 Mark: Those per-request numbers — what are GPU-hours assumptions?
05:51 Lena: Assumes p3-like baseline for hosted and mps/our optimized kernels for Dedicated. We include kernel selection overheads and KV memory RPC costs in a conservative way.
06:08 Aisha: How accurate are these for our peak flash-sale patterns? We'll have big concurrency spikes.
06:15 Diego: For spiky workloads we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity or using smart routing to route spikes to hosted pool to protect p95. Also autoscaling policies with warm-up buffers. We'll share recommended autoscale settings.
06:33 Priya: Also encryption — can caching live in customer VPC only? We need to ensure KV doesn't leave our network.
06:41 Samir: Private deployments or Dedicated with Private VPC placement can ensure KV and prefix cache stay in your VPC; we support customer-managed KMS. We'll flag required configs in the security pack.
06:55 [pause, short hold music noise from one attendee]
07:20 Lena: Quick demo: I'll show a small request stream and toggle prefix cache on/off to show token counts.
07:30 [screen noise]
07:36 Lena: With prefix cache off: tokens generated per request = 120, latency p95 = 220ms under the demo load. With prefix cache on and 50% prefix reuse: tokens generated 72, p95 drops to 170ms. These are demo env numbers.
08:02 Aisha: That p95 drop is the kind we need.
08:07 Mark: Any quality regressions when you use prefix cache? I'm worried about caching stale context or mismatched prompts.
08:15 Diego: Good point — prefix cache keys are content hashes; if prompt templates change we invalidate cache. For multi-turn dialogs we attach TTLs and versioning. We also support targeted invalidation via API.
08:37 Aisha: What about privacy — do you store user data in caches?
08:41 Samir: We can configure caches to be ephemeral and not persisted to disk, and in Private mode you control access. We'll include data retention options in the security docs.
09:00 Mark: Ok, onboarding — how long to get Dedicated with our VPC?
09:06 Samir: Typical timeline: 4-6 weeks for Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS integration for enterprise accounts; a pilot on a staged cluster can be 1-2 weeks.
09:18 Priya: We prefer a 2-week pilot in staging first.
09:22 Samir: Sounds good — we'll scope a 2-week benchmark. Lena, can you outline the test plan?
09:29 Lena: Yes. We'll need: sample prompt distribution, target concurrency patterns, a staging token to run against, and a success criteria doc — p95 under 200ms and cost per request targets. We'll run runs with and without prefix cache and with different batch sizes.
09:47 Aisha: We'll send distributions today.
09:50 Diego: Also will include KV cache memory tuning and a run for partial-match reuse.
10:02 Mark: For billing — will the pilot be free or discounted?
10:05 Samir: We typically offer pilot credits; we'll confirm in follow-up email and the spreadsheet.
10:12 [pause]
10:20 Aisha: A few nitty-gritty Qs: do you support SAML SSO for console access? We need RBAC and audit trails for token-level tracing.
10:29 Samir: Yes SAML/SSO, RBAC roles, and token-level analytics in Console. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM. We'll attach docs.
10:38 Priya: KMS integration — hardware HSM support?
10:41 Diego: We integrate with customer KMS and can talk about HSM-backed keys for enterprise plans. Specifics in security packet.
10:51 Aisha: Any limitations around prompt length and KV? Some of our backfill jobs go to 5k tokens.
10:57 Lena: For long sequences KV costs grow linearly; for very long sequences we suggest chunking or specialized pipelines. We'll annotate recommended thresholds per model size.
11:14 Mark: If we do prefix cache + batching, do we see compounding savings or diminishing returns?
11:20 Lena: Usually compounding to an extent — prefix cache reduces the tokens generated which reduces model runtime; batching then improves throughput on what's left. But if prefix cache reduces tokens a lot, batching gains shrink because there's less to batch. The cost model table shows diminishing slope.
11:40 Aisha: Can you show an example for our highest-value flow — the fraud scoring microflow?
11:46 Lena: Yes, row 12 in the spreadsheet: avg 120 tokens, 60% prefix reuse, batch size 32 in nightly batch jobs yields 55% cost reduction vs baseline. For real-time path batch size 8 and prefix 50% yields ~35% cost reduction.
12:02 Samir: We'll export that sheet and tailor it with your actual metrics.
12:09 [brief side conversation, muted mics]
12:30 Mark: About fallbacks — if a model variant fails or capacity is full, what's routing policy?
12:36 Diego: Redwood supports smart routing: prioritize latency SLO routes to Dedicated; if capacity constrained, fallback to a smaller model or hosted pool. You can configure canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies.
12:53 Aisha: For scoring we need deterministic behavior; how do rollbacks affect scoring variance?
12:59 Lena: We version models and keep stable variants pinned for scoring. Any fallback would be to a validated variant with recorded eval differences; we'll flag regressions and allow auto-reject if quality delta exceeds your threshold.
13:18 Priya: Any further security proof points? Pen test reports?
13:22 Samir: We'll attach SOC2, pen test summary, and network architecture for Private/Dedicated.
13:32 Aisha: Good. Timeline: we aim for pilot in two weeks and production in 8 weeks if pilot passes.
13:40 Samir: Noted. We'll action the spreadsheet and security pack.
13:46 [longer demo playback snippets]
20:05 Lena: Quick note on observability — Console shows per-route latency, token-level cost, and KV hit rates. That helps set TTLs and batching knobs.
20:23 Mark: Will we get SDKs for our Java platform?
20:27 Samir: Yes we have official SDKs for Python, Node, Java, and gRPC interfaces. We'll link repo.
20:36 Aisha: A little worried about transcription — oh sorry, I mean multi-region failover. We need EU residency for some customers.
20:45 Diego: Redwood supports region pinning and can keep data in EU regions for hosted; Private can be on-prem.
20:54 Priya: For pilot we need a staging EU region run.
20:58 Samir: We'll plan that.
21:10 [people mute/unmute chatter as they move to laptops]
21:32 Lena: Back to cost model: I'll walk through sensitivity analysis: varying prefix match rate from 10% to 70% and batch size from 8 to 128. The spreadsheet computes cost per 1M requests.
21:50 Lena: For your baseline traffic shape, most savings come from increasing prefix reuse (e.g., templating prompts) and tuning small bounded batches for the real-time path. Big batches best for async/backfill.
22:12 Aisha: Are there recommended prompt engineering changes to increase prefix reuse?
22:18 Diego: Yes — normalize templates, move user-specific fields to post-processing where possible, or use structured function calls instead of free text. That increases exact-match reuse.
22:33 Mark: Could we accidentally break quality if we over-normalize?
22:37 Diego: Possibly — we'll run evals on a holdout set to ensure changes don't increase false positives in fraud scoring. Part of the pilot.
22:50 Samir: Any other questions?
22:55 Aisha: One last on billing unit: do you bill generated tokens or input+output?
23:00 Lena: We bill for generated tokens for generation endpoints; for embeddings it's per vector. The spreadsheet will show both ways for clarity.
23:12 Mark: Ok. Also want to review SLA for Dedicated.
23:16 Samir: We'll attach SLA doc.
23:21 [silence, someone types]
23:45 Samir: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send tailored cost model and security pack, Lena will run benchmark plan, Novafinance will send distributions, and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff next week.
24:02 Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
24:07 Priya: Thanks.
24:10 Lena: Thanks all.
